title: How many fold lines does this dot pattern have?
description: A large six sided dot pattern made of star shapes repeats its design round the centre. Its fold lines are found by testing straight and slanted folds through the centre.
teaching_notes: One idea: look for lines through the centre where one side matches the other, and test each by folding, rather than guessing from the repeats. Watch for students who forget the slanted lines.

source: Find the lines of symmetry for the {{NAME_1}} below.
video_script.why: The child searches a larger pattern for straight and slanted fold lines through its centre.
video_script.substitution: Look for lines through the centre where one side matches the other, and test each by folding.
video_script.anchor: A large six sided dot pattern with star shapes that repeat round the centre
video_script.payoff_line: Test every line through the centre, straight and slanted.

final_answer.value: 6 lines: one vertical, one horizontal and four slanted
final_answer.spoken: six lines, one vertical, one horizontal and four slanted, all through the centre

names.{{NAME_1}}: traditional dot pattern whose lines of symmetry are to be found

hold_back: one vertical, one horizontal and four slanted
never_show: the total before the folds are made
maths_rules: A line of symmetry is a fold line along which one half covers the other exactly.
The pattern repeats six times round its centre, which suggests six lines but must be tested by folding.
The matching folds are one vertical, one horizontal and four slanted, all through the centre.
Check: fold along each of the six lines once more.
video_script.design: One idea: test straight and slanted folds through the centre of a pattern. Assumes the child knows the fold test. The pattern stays on the board from the hook to the end.
open_questions: The pattern is described in the worklist as a six sided dot pattern of star shapes made of diamonds, and the six lines (one vertical, one horizontal, four slanted) are taken from the worklist, since the printed figure could not be seen.
